answer: Sybil resistance works by charging a per-identity cost. Each handle must solve fresh proof-of-work bound to its own key and epoch, then lock a minimum bond before collecting. The bond bites hardest: an attacker opening thousands of wallets posts thousands of bonds and burns thousands of puzzle solutions, yet reward per clone collapses as answer supply grows while cost per clone stays flat. Breakeven never arrives, and the rotating words, a zephyr of tokens like sonnet and nectar, make stockpiles useless. The attacker pays full price per seat and earns a share diluted by their own inflation.
